messages.text: Djokovic creates more history with epic Zverev win at China Open

metadata.summary: Novak Djokovic rolled back the years to defeat French Open and US Open champion Alexander Zverev 4-6 6-4 6-4 to reach the semi-finals of the China Open on Sunday.
metadata.content: China Open: Novak Djokovic keeps unblemished record in Beijing by handing Alexander Zverev a rare defeat | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content China Open: Novak Djokovic keeps unblemished record in Beijing by handing Alexander Zverev a rare defeat Novak Djokovic preserves his unblemished record in Beijing by downing in-form Alexander Zverev to set up a semi-final showdown with Daniil Medvedev; you can watch the WTA/ATP China Open and ATP 1000 Shanghai Masters live on Sky Sports Sunday 4 October 2026 15:35, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Novak Djokovic and Alexander Zverev served up an unbelievable rally during their clash at the China Open Novak Djokovic rolled back the years to defeat French Open and US Open champion Alexander Zverev 4-6 6-4 6-4 to reach the semi-finals of the China Open on Sunday. The 39-year-old Serbian created a new piece of tennis history with the best start in men's singles at a tour-level event in the Open Era as he moved to 32-0 in Beijing. With his victory, Djokovic moved past Rafael Nadal for the best start at a single event, with Nadal having won his first 31 matches at the French Open. messages.text: Daryz retains Arc crown with dazzling display

metadata.summary: Daryz became the first colt for almost 50 years to win Europe’s most prestigious race, the Qatar Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe, in successive seasons with a brilliant victory at ParisLongchamp.
metadata.content: Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe: Daryz becomes first colt since 1978 to retain Group 1 crown | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe: Daryz becomes first colt since 1978 to retain Group 1 crown The Francis-Henri Graffard-trained Daryz became the first colt since 1978 to retain his Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe crown with a magnificent performance at ParisLongchamp; Bay City Roller finished runner-up, with Diamond Necklace third Sunday 4 October 2026 16:20, UK Image: Daryz won the 2026 Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe Daryz became the first colt for almost 50 years to win Europe’s most prestigious race, the Qatar Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe, in successive seasons with a brilliant victory at ParisLongchamp. Not since the Vincent O'Brien-trained Alleged and Lester Piggott in 1977 and 1978 has a colt managed to defend his title, but once Mickael Barzalona pulled the Francis-Henri Graffard-trained Daryz out to make his run the result looked inevitable. The Prix Foy proved the key form guide, as Daryz beat George Scott's Bay City Roller in that trial and those two filled the same positions again in the main event, with Aidan O'Brien's Diamond Necklace running a fine race in third from stall 16. Barzalona said: "To win this kind of race twice proves that Daryz is an exceptional horse. messages.text: Meronk outlasts Jarvis to win Alfred Dunhill Links Championship

metadata.summary: Adrian Meronk came from four shots behind to overtake Casey Jarvis and win the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship by two shots on a gripping final day at St Andrews.
metadata.content: Alfred Dunhill Links Championship: LIV Golf’s Adrian Meronk outlasts Casey Jarvis to claim victory at St Andrews | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Alfred Dunhill Links Championship: LIV Golf’s Adrian Meronk outlasts Casey Jarvis to claim victory at St Andrews Adrian Meronk ended a 1,087-wait to win his fifth DP World Tour Title as he surged past Casey Jarvis to win the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship by two shots; watch next week's Open de Espana live on Sky Sports Golf from Thursday at 1pm Ed Carruthers Digital Sports Journalist Sunday 4 October 2026 18:02, UK Image: Adrian Meronk held off overnight leader Casey Jarvis to win the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship Adrian Meronk came from four shots behind to overtake Casey Jarvis and win the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship by two shots on a gripping final day at St Andrews. The victory saw the LIV Golfer end a 1,078-day wait to claim his fifth DP World Tour title and regain his tour card for next season, as the Polish golfer posted a final-round score of 68.
